item.content:encoded:
Really neat! I love the format and am curious if the author has some degree of background in biomedical or the like. The ambition suits the GOI well, too.

Gotta agree with everyone saying the costs are too low by an order of magnitude, though. I've worked in some basic research myself and everything is stupid expensive. The animal testing I could buy if they're being shady/sloppy, but most of the equipment would have to be custom made, multiplying the cost. For reference, a bog-standard MRI machine still goes for about a million (plus hundreds of thousands more for the room it sits in), and a steel crucible you'd find in a factory is closer to 15 mil.

Regardless, you get some degree of belief-stretching artistic license with this sort of thing. The whole associated set of entries make for a fun read.

item.content:encoded:
A few notes on costs:

  • First off, this is written back in the late 80s. While inflation hasn't been bad enough that money was worth an order of magnitude more back then, money was definitely worth more back then than it is now.
  • Second, PL has access to resources that many organizations don't. Who knows what kind of cost-cutting paratech they have lying around.
  • Third, costs are going to tend to be on the optimistic side, while still being within realistic (for PL) estimates. This'll drop the numbers a bit.

Well that was enjoyable. Nothing like a shady laboratory asking for a ludicrous amount of cash for possibly clandestine purposes.

Like I said in chat, parts of this do drag a bit, but I feel that is more do the the style of this format, as there is only so much excitement you can fit into a scientific grant proposal. Still, the addition of the picture is a nice touch.

+1. Good job.
